one_liner: Igor Pavlov's public-domain LZMA/LZMA2 codec behind 7-Zip: 11% smaller than bzip2 -9, 2.2x faster decoding, 5x slower compression.
what_it_does: The LZMA SDK is the reference C encoder and decoder for LZMA (LZ77 plus an adaptive binary range coder) and LZMA2 (the chunked wrapper used inside .7z and .xz); in ip7z/7zip it is the public-domain subset of the C/ directory next to the LGPL 7-Zip archiver. The API is buffer-to-buffer (LzmaEncode/LzmaDecode, or the LzmaCompress/LzmaUncompress wrapper in LzmaLib.h with a 5-byte properties blob), streaming through ISeqInStream/ISeqOutStream callbacks (LzmaEnc_Encode) or a zlib-like decode loop (LzmaDec_DecodeToBuf), plus Lzma2Enc/Lzma2DecMt for LZMA2 with optional threads. Callers pass their own ISzAlloc allocators. It is not a drop-in for bzip2: different format, different API.
how_it_is_fast: Against bzip2 the decoder wins because it does no block sort to undo: it decodes one bit at a time with a range coder against context-selected probabilities (literal context bits lc/lp, position bits pb, rep-match state machine) and copies matches out of a window of up to 256 MB at the default -9 on 64-bit. The ratio comes from that large window plus near-optimal parsing over a binary-tree (bt4) match finder at levels 5-9 (hash chains and a fast parser at 0-4). The per-bit range decoding is also why it tops out near 60-80 MB/s single-threaded. Speed-ups beyond the portable C: SSE4.1/AVX2/NEON match-finder normalisation, a second match-finder thread (LzFindMt), and hand-written x64 and arm64 decoders (LzmaDecOpt), which src-history 18.03 says run about 30% faster than the C decoder.
when_to_use: Compress-once, read-many artifacts where size matters more than decode speed: in lzbench 2.4, lzma -9 is 10.8% smaller than bzip2 -9 and 28% smaller than zlib -9 on silesia.tar, and it decodes at 78 MB/s.

Replacing bzip2 when you can change the format: at equal output size, lzma -0 compresses 2.2x and decompresses 1.5x faster than bzip2 -1, and lzma -4 is 1.07x and 2.1x faster than bzip2 -9 at 2.5% larger output (derived from page data). lzma -6 is the usual sweet spot (3.13 / 78.4 MB/s, only 1.8% larger than -9).

When you need dependency-free, public-domain code to read or write raw LZMA, LZMA2 or .7z streams inside a C or C++ program. The decoder is LzmaDec.c plus four headers, uses 200-400 bytes of stack and 16 KB of state plus the dictionary.
Embedded or installer decompression where code size and decoder memory matter more than throughput (Z7_LZMA_SIZE_OPT shrinks the decoder further).
Builds where you can assemble 7-Zip's LzmaDecOpt (x64 via asmc or UASM, arm64 via GNU as) to recover the roughly 30-50% decode speed that a C-only build gives up.
when_not_to_use: Decode-heavy workloads: in the same lzbench table zstd 1.5.7 -18 decodes 15x faster (1175 vs 78.2 MB/s) at 9.5% larger output, brotli -11 4.9x faster at 3.5% larger, zlib -9 4.1x faster at 39% larger, and LZHAM -1 3.5x faster at 12% larger (derived from page data).

Compression throughput: -9 runs at 2.55 MB/s on one thread. bzip3 -5 compresses 4.7x faster with 3% smaller output, though it decodes 6.3x slower. Fast LZMA2 -10 writes the same LZMA2 format at the same size 1.33x faster.

Memory-limited encoders: the encoder needs about dictSize x 11.5 + 6 MB, which is about 2.9 GB at the 64-bit -9 default (256 MB dictionary). The decoder needs the whole dictionary unless it decodes straight into a full-size output buffer with LzmaDecode.

Plain .xz handling: liblzma (xz 5.8.4) writes and reads the container with integrity checks and decodes faster in lzbench (122 vs 78.2 MB/s, partly an asm-versus-C build difference). The raw .lzma format has no checksum.
Projects that cannot audit licences file by file: the repository is LGPL-2.1+ with BSD and unRAR-restricted parts; only the files whose header says 'Public domain' are free to copy.

integration.form: source-drop (C files from C/: LzmaDec, LzmaEnc, LzFind, LzFindMt, LzFindOpt, Lzma2*, Threads, CpuArch plus headers; 7-Zip's site also ships them as a separate LZMA SDK archive)
integration.dependencies: none; POSIX or Win32 threads for LzFindMt, Lzma2DecMt and MtCoder unless built with Z7_ST
integration.min_toolchain: Portable C; DOC/readme.txt lists MSVC 6.0 through VS2022, GCC and Clang; lzbench builds it with gcc 15.2.0 -std=gnu99. The optional asm decoder needs asmc or UASM for x64 MASM syntax, or GNU as for arm64.
integration.platforms: any (x86, x86-64, ARM, ARM64 and others); SSE4.1/AVX2/NEON match-finder paths chosen at run time; asm decoders for x64 and arm64 only
integration.thread_safety: Each CLzmaEnc, CLzmaDec or Lzma2 handle is independent and allocators are passed per call. The only process global is the SIMD function pointer that LzFindPrepare() sets. By default the encoder starts its own match-finder thread at levels 5-9.

gotchas: Defaults differ from the header docs. LzmaLib.h (dated 2023-04-02) still lists 64 MB for level 9, but LzmaEncProps_Normalize (changed in 24.09 per src-history) gives 32/64/128/256/256 MB for levels 5-9 on 64-bit. Unless reduceSize or Lzma2Enc_SetDataSize is set, the stream advertises that dictionary and the decoder allocates all of it. lzbench never sets it, so its -9 row uses a 256 MB window, against 64 MiB for xz -9.

LzmaEncode and LzmaCompress default to numThreads = 2 in normal mode (levels 5-9), so a 'single-threaded' call spawns a match-finder thread. Set numThreads = 1 or build with Z7_ST. lzbench forces one thread through numTotalThreads = 1, so its compression figures are truly single-threaded.

Harness asymmetry in lzbench: the lzma row is the C decoder (no Z7_LZMA_DEC_OPT or LzmaDecOpt.asm), while the xz 5.8.4 row gets liblzma's x86-64 inline-asm range decoder by default (range_decoder.h picks LZMA_RANGE_DECODER_CONFIG 0x1F0 for GCC/Clang, and lzbench's hand-written config.h does not override it). ip7z/7zip issue #11 measured the asm decoder 1.53x faster than C (7z b on an Intel N100: 68.6 vs 44.9 MB/s), so most of the 122 vs 78.2 MB/s gap to xz is a build difference. The bzip2 comparison is C against C and stands. Decode timing also includes a per-call dictionary allocation and an extra memcpy of input and output through Lzma2DecMt's 1 MB stream buffers: a small cost at 78 MB/s (estimate).

The .lzma 'alone' header (properties, dictionary size, uncompressed size) carries no checksum, so verify integrity yourself or use .xz/.7z. Vendored copies do not get 7-Zip's security fixes: 26.02 fixed CVE-2026-14266, a heap overflow in XZ chunked-data handling (from search snippets; which file was fixed is not documented in src-history). LzFindPrepare() must be called once by the application to enable the SIMD match-finder normalisation; the library never calls it.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick the LZMA SDK over libbzip2 or lbzip2 whenever the format is yours to choose (11% smaller and 2.2x faster decoding at -9), and over xz/liblzma when you need public-domain raw LZMA, LZMA2 or .7z code or the smallest embeddable decoder. For .xz files prefer liblzma; for faster compression to the same LZMA2 stream prefer Fast LZMA2; for decode speed at a similar ratio prefer LZHAM or zstd -18.
verified_claims_summary: lzbench 2.4 (release binary built with gcc 15.2.0 at -O3, one thread of an AMD EPYC 9555P at 3.20 GHz with turbo off, silesia.tar of 211,947,520 bytes) measured lzma 26.03 -9 at 2.55 MB/s compress and 78.2 MB/s decompress with 48,682,482 bytes of output, against bzip2 1.0.8 -9 at 12.7 / 35.5 MB/s and 54,572,811 bytes: 2.2x faster decoding, 10.8% smaller output and 5.0x slower compression. At matched size, lzma -0 against bzip2 -1 is 2.2x faster to compress and 1.5x faster to decode (derived from page data). lzbench encodes an LZMA2 stream with Lzma2Enc_Encode2 (numTotalThreads = 1) and decodes it with Lzma2DecMt_Decode using the C decoder only; every run is memcmp-checked against the input.
status_note: Actively maintained: 7-Zip 26.04 is dated 2026-10-05 in C/7zVersion.h and ip7z/7zip mirrors each release as one commit (4.1k stars, 169 open issues). The LZMA SDK files are public domain and easy to vendor, but the rest of the repository is LGPL-2.1+ with BSD and unRAR parts, so copy only files whose header says 'Public domain'.
